title: How Vorys Transitioned to Flo’s ATS with Historical Data
summary: Elizabeth Greiner, Content Manager at Flo Recruit, sat down with Anna D’Alesandro, Legal Recruiting and Integration Coordinator and Kayla Allen, Senior Manager - Legal Talent Development at Vorys, to discuss their transition from spreadsheets and a custom Access Database to Flo Recruit Applicant Tracking for law student, lateral associate, partner, and patent professional recruitment.
body_text: Elizabeth Greiner, Content Manager at Flo Recruit, sat down with Anna D’Alesandro, Legal Recruiting and Integration Coordinator and Kayla Allen, Senior Manager - Legal Talent Development at Vorys, to discuss their transition from spreadsheets and a custom Access Database to Flo Recruit Applicant Tracking for law student, lateral associate, partner, and patent professional recruitment. With a focus on streamlining processes, saving time, and creating custom models to synthesize hiring data, Vorys has redefined its recruiting operations with Flo – including bringing years of historical candidate data into the new ATS for centralized access. Q: Can you each tell us about your role at Vorys? Anna: I’ve been at Vorys for four years, and I serve as the Legal Recruiting and Integration Coordinator. My primary focus is supporting lateral attorney hiring, from interviews through onboarding, for candidates with a year or more of experience. Before this recent switch to the lateral side, I managed the hiring for our summer program, including all 1L hiring. I have seen all aspects of our recruiting and hiring process. Kayla: I’ve been with the firm for 17 years, and I am the Senior Manager of Legal Talent Development. In my current role, I manage our attorney and patent professional training and development programs and collaborate on career development initiatives to enhance legal talent retention, engagement and well-being. Anna and I worked closely to bring Flo Recruit into the firm, and together we’ve seen how much it’s changed the way we operate. Q: What was your recruiting process like before Flo? Kayla: Before Flo, we didn’t have an ATS. Everything lived in Excel spreadsheets and an Access Database. For a firm of our size, that system just wasn’t sustainable. We knew we needed to do better, so we started exploring vendors, and Flo stood out as the most user-friendly and flexible option. It felt like the right next step, and looking back, it absolutely was. Anna: From a time management perspective, the challenges became particularly evident during the OCI season. We were juggling data from a dozen OCI programs and over 40 resume collects, all while trying to manage it in spreadsheets. It just wasn’t feasible. Since adopting Flo, everything has been streamlined, from applications flowing in through schools and direct applications, to candidate reviews, to the packets we prepare for our attorneys. Q: How has Flo Recruit Applicant Tracking changed your day-to-day work? Kayla: The data has been a game-changer. Before Flo, we were compiling numbers from so many different places and hoping they were right. With Flo, the reporting capabilities are astounding. The visuals give our partners exactly what they’ve been asking for, and we can export real-time data to share instantly. We’ve even been able to grant access to hiring committee members so they can view candidate information directly in the system, which saves us time as well. Anna: For me, the Candidate Review feature has been huge. It makes it so easy to organize feedback and keep everything in one place. The efficiencies we’ve gained are undeniable. Kayla: The time savings and efficiency are just huge. It used to take two people to keep this all going, and now one person can handle it, because of Flo. We’ve significantly reduced the administrative burdens of the recruitment process utilizing this platform, and as a result, we’ve been able to shift our focus to more strategic initiatives, which has allowed us to bring more value to our talent operations. Q: How did the historical data transfer process go? Anna: It was so much easier than we expected. Flo provided a simple spreadsheet template that matched exactly what we needed. I filled it in, sent it to the Flo support team, and they uploaded it the same day. It couldn’t have been smoother. Kayla: We thought transferring thousands of records would be overwhelming, but Flo made us so comfortable and came up with a simple plan. They explained exactly how we needed to provide the data and assured us that we could make it all work. We did face one challenge — we hadn’t consistently stored candidate emails — but Flo came up with a creative workaround. The solution made it seamless, and now everything, including historical data, is so easy to access. Q: How do you use historical data today? Anna: It’s incredibly simple. If I need to look up a historical candidate record, I can easily pull it up in our database and keep everything connected to our current tracking. There’s no more digging through spreadsheets or trying to locate old information. Kayla: It’s all consolidated in one place now, which has streamlined our process tremendously. The ability to reference historical information, while also keeping our current system easily updated is so simple. Q: What was your experience with Flo’s support team? Anna: I can’t say enough good things about everyone I’ve interacted with at Flo! Whether through the chat or email, they’re always quick to respond and incredibly helpful. During our onboarding, I always felt like they met us where we were and made everything work for what we needed, and at our pace. It was all so intuitive, and we were supported every step of the way. Kayla: We’ve had such a positive experience. If we ever have a question or request, the team is always receptive. They collaborate with us, take feedback seriously, and continue to evolve the product in smart ways. That responsiveness has been invaluable. Q: Looking back, what advice would you give to another firm considering Flo or with any concerns about the data transfer? Anna: It feels like a bigger project than it actually is. Flo helps you break the process into manageable steps and always finds solutions to any challenge. Kayla: The upfront investment of time and planning is absolutely worth it. Once you see everything in one place, you’ll wonder how you ever managed before. For us, there’s no going back to spreadsheets. Q: You also recently launched your Flo Forward profile. What impact has that had? Anna: The impact was immediate. As soon as our profile went live, I noticed students applying to our 2026 summer associate program and listing Flo Forward as their source. It was great validation that students are actively using the platform to research firms. Kayla: We’re really excited to see how much Flo Forward continues to influence our recruiting. It’s been a strong start, and we’re eager to build on that momentum. Conclusion By adopting Flo Recruit for all recruitment, from summers to partners, Vorys has transformed its recruiting process — moving away from outdated spreadsheets and databases and toward a streamlined, data-driven approach. The firm has saved time, redefined team roles, and gained new insights into its recruiting operations. While the switch to a new system, and the historical data transfer that comes with that, can feel daunting, working with Flo and preparing upfront made the transition simple.

title: Airship AI Announces $11.0 Million of Firm Fixed Price Brand Name Only Awards from US Federal Law Enforcement Agencies in September

body_text: Airship AI Announces $11.0 Million of Firm Fixed Price Brand Name Only Awards from US Federal Law Enforcement Agencies in September October 06, 2025 8:31 AM EDT Download as PDF Public Safety and Homeland Security Macro Tailwinds Remain Strong Heading into the US Federal Government’s Fiscal First Quarter REDMOND, Wash., Oct. 06, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Airship AI Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: AISP) (“Airship AI” or the “Company”), a leader in AI-driven video, sensor, and data management surveillance solutions, today announced it has been awarded 16 individual contracts from agencies within the Department of Justice (“DOJ”) and Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”) for Airship’s AI driven technical solutions supporting public safety and investigative requirements. “These awards reflect the continued momentum and critical importance of AI-driven surveillance solutions in advancing public safety and homeland security,” said Paul Allen, President of Airship AI. “As the administration prioritizes strengthening national security, AI is proving to be an essential force multiplier for law enforcement, delivering greater operational efficiency, enhanced accuracy, and improved threat detection, particularly along the border.” Airship AI delivers a full spectrum of solutions, ranging from advanced analytics at the edge to datacenter and cloud-based AI capabilities. By aggregating thousands of edge-generated feeds into a unified “single pane of glass,” Airship AI provides real-time alerts on suspicious activity and events at both regional and national scales. These capabilities enable agencies to maximize existing resources, with AI serving as the first set of eyes, automatically detecting potential threats so operators can focus attention where it is needed most. At the core of these capabilities is Outpost AI , Airship AI’s advanced edge-based appliance. Outpost AI leverages proprietary, in-house trained models to detect a wide range of user-defined objects and events. Its integrated rule engine allows agencies to predefine autonomous actions, such as automatically tracking an item of interest, without requiring constant human oversight. With a compact form factor and minimal power requirements, Outpost AI is seamlessly integrated into both new and existing systems, transforming traditional sensor packages into intelligent, autonomous solutions at a fraction of the cost of full replacement. “These recent awards not only reinforce and expand our existing deployed capabilities but also open the door to significant new requirements where Airship AI's solution stack has clearly demonstrated its ability to address additional agency challenges,” continued Mr. Allen. “In one case, following several successful pilot deployments that replaced underperforming competitive systems, our platform was adopted as the preferred solution for all future related infrastructure requirements.” Mr. Allen added, “Beyond these awards, we are actively pursuing a large number of opportunities whose funding shifted from the fourth quarter into the first quarter of the government’s fiscal year, as well as new opportunities that emerged in the third quarter, opportunities that will further expand Airship AI's footprint supporting mission critical operations across the federal law enforcement community.” About Airship AI Holdings, Inc. Founded in 2006, Airship AI (NASDAQ: AISP) is a U.S. owned and operated technology company headquartered in Redmond, Washington. Airship AI is an AI-driven video, sensor and data management surveillance platform that improves public safety and operational efficiency for public sector and commercial customers by providing predictive analysis of events before they occur and meaningful intelligence to decision makers. Airship AI’s product suite includes Outpost AI edge hardware and software offerings, Acropolis enterprise management software stack, and Command family of visualization tools. title: DIY vs. Professional Painting: When to Hire a Pro
summary: Painting your home can be a big project. Let's make sure it's done professionally.
body_text: DIY vs. Professional Painting: When to Hire a Pro Painting your home can be a big project. Let's make sure it's done professionally. Embarking on a home improvement journey is an exciting endeavor, especially when you have a plethora of drool-worthy pins you've been saving on Pinterest. From Kevin Francis O’Gara to Joanna Gaines to Charlotte's very own Holly Phillip's The English Room , we all desire a home that could be featured in Architectural Digest . But are we capable of weighing the pros and cons of DIY painting to achieve the look? The inspiration for the Drawing Room paint color in the Magnolia Home by Joanna Gaines Castle Collection stems from the inherent elegance and timeless style of the room itself. Crafted to reflect the sophistication and enduring allure of the space, this color choice embodies the design ethos of Magnolia Home, curated by Joanna Gaines. Photo courtesy of: kilz.com. The inspiration for the Drawing Room paint color in the Magnolia Home by Joanna Gaines Castle Collection stems from the inherent elegance and timeless style of the room itself. Crafted to reflect the sophistication and enduring allure of the space, this color choice embodies the design ethos of Magnolia Home, curated by Joanna Gaines. Photo courtesy of: kilz.com . Now I'll be the first to say that I love a good DIY project. If there is a cheaper way I can achieve the look of my favorite interior designers, count me in. I have painted three out of five rooms in my house and did I have fun while doing it? Some of the time. Let's just say two of those rooms I have already repainted because I couldn't find the right color and one of the rooms is still not 100% finished. Not to mention the paint-stained tile. As much as I hate to say it, achieving an Architectural Digest-worthy home necessitates a level of expertise and precision that extends beyond the realm of DIY projects. A professional painting company brings a wealth of experience, a keen eye for detail, and the knowledge to navigate complex design challenges. From selecting the perfect color palette to executing intricate finishes, their skill set transforms a space into a masterpiece. When aiming for a home that graces the pages of Architectural Digest, the investment in a professional painting company is not just a practical choice; it's a strategic one that guarantees a result synonymous with luxury and refined taste. To help convince you, let's dive into the intricacies of both DIY and professional painting and why the latter might be the superior choice for homeowners in the Queen City. DIY Painting Variety of paint colors as swatches. The DIY Appeal 1. Cost Savings At first glance, the appeal of a DIY paint job lies in the potential cost savings. By purchasing your painting supplies, you have more control over the budget, making it seem like a more financially prudent option. 2. Personal Touch DIY projects offer a canvas for personal expression. Homeowners can select colors, patterns, and styles that resonate with their unique taste, fostering a sense of ownership over the living space. 3. Sense of Accomplishment Completing a DIY painting project can provide a profound sense of accomplishment. The tangible result of your efforts can be a source of pride and satisfaction, showcasing your skills and dedication to your home. The Pitfalls of DIY Painting 1. Time-Consuming DIY painting projects are notorious for taking longer than anticipated. Balancing work, family, and other responsibilities can turn what seemed like a weekend project into a prolonged endeavor. Surface preparation is actually over 50% of the job. If you have a small space, then way the pros and cons of DIY painting yourself. 2. Skill and Precision Achieving a professional-looking finish requires skill and precision with the right painting techniques. Without the proper techniques and tools, DIY painters may struggle to produce seamless and even results, leading to frustration and disappointment. 3. Potential Mistakes The learning curve in DIY projects often includes making mistakes. While these mistakes are part of the learning process, rectifying errors can be costly in terms of both time and money. It is difficult to master the proper paint application that is needed for your project. Charlotte's Interior Design Influence Kathy Smith Designs Chic Interior in Charlotte, North Carolina. Photo courtesy of Southern Home Magazine. Kathy Smith Designs Chic Interior in Charlotte, North Carolina. Photo courtesy of Southern Home Magazine. 1. Charlotte's Distinctive Aesthetics Drive around Charlotte and you can't help but gawk at the homes in Dilworth, Myers Park, and Plaza Midwood . All with its own, unique historic charm, this city boasts homes that are a testament to quality design. If your home is situated in these neighborhoods, aligning with its distinctive aesthetics becomes crucial. A professional painter with an understanding of the neighborhood's unique characteristics can bring out the best in your home's design. I own a 1945 Southern-style cottage and it's gorgeous inside and out. With an older home, my design aesthetic had to shift as I wanted to preserve the historic charm of the interior and exterior. Some complementary paint colors I used were Lakeside , Soft Sage , and Mauve Rose . Home by Charlotte, North Carolina's Charlotte Lucas. Home by Charlotte, North Carolina's Charlotte Lucas . 2. Inspiration from Interior Designers: Charlotte is home to renowned interior designers, and their work is evident in various neighborhoods. I mean wouldn't we all like to live in a living room designed by Kathy Smith ? Drawing inspiration from these professionals means aiming for a finish that aligns with the high standards set by design enthusiasts. Achieving such precision is often better left in the hands of seasoned professionals. Professional Painting The Professional Advantage: Why Hire a Pro? 1. Complex Surfaces Require Expertise Pro painters bring a level of expertise that is particularly beneficial when dealing with complex surfaces. Whether it's textured walls, ornate trims, or intricate details, a professional painter can navigate these challenges with finesse, ensuring a flawless finish that DIY endeavors may struggle to achieve with their painting tools. 2. Time Constraints Demand Efficiency Busy schedules are a reality for many homeowners. The time constraints imposed by work, family obligations, and social commitments may not allow for the luxury of dedicating extended periods to your paint projects. Hiring a professional ensures a quicker turnaround, allowing you to enjoy your freshly painted space sooner without sacrificing quality. 3. Quality Assurance Professional painters prioritize quality assurance and painting techniques. With years of experience, they understand the nuances of various surfaces and know how to prepare and apply paint for a lasting finish. This commitment to quality paint application ensures that your home receives a level of precision and durability that may be challenging to achieve with a DIY approach. Craftwork painter painting a white wall with pink trim. 4. Extensive Projects Demand Professionalism For large-scale projects involving multiple rooms or an entire house, the efficiency and expertise of a professional painting contractor become even more apparent. They can manage the logistics of extensive projects, ensuring a cohesive and uniform finish throughout the entire interior painting space. 5. Access to Premium Products Professional painters often have access to premium paint products and finishes that may not be readily available to the general public. These high-quality painting tools contribute to a superior finish and greater longevity for your painted surface, especially for an exterior paint job. Conclusion A Brush with Professional Excellence Choosing Craftwork over tackling the project yourself ensures a seamless and high-quality transformation for your space. Our team of skilled artisans brings years of expertise to every job, guaranteeing meticulous attention to detail and a flawless finish. We understand that painting involves more than just applying color; it requires careful surface preparation, knowledge of the right materials, and efficient execution. By entrusting your project to Craftwork, you save valuable time and effort, allowing you to focus on what matters most to you. We use premium paints and tools, ensuring a durable and long-lasting result for interior painting or an exterior paint job. Additionally, our commitment to customer satisfaction means we work closely with you, offering personalized consultations and accommodating your preferences. Craftwork does not just offer professional painting services; it's a dedication to turning your vision into a beautifully painted reality with professionalism and precision.

title: Estrella Immunopharma Regains Compliance with Nasdaq Listing Requirements | EstrellaImmunopharma
body_text: Emeryville, California, October 6, 2025 – Estrella Immunopharma, Inc. (NASDAQ: ESLA) (“Estrella” or the “Company”), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company developing CD19 and CD22-targeted ARTEMIS ® T-cell therapies to treat cancer and autoimmune diseases, announces that, as previously disclosed in its Current Report on Form 8-K filed on September 29, 2025, the Company has regained compliance with the listing requirements of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”). This confirmation follows the Company’s successful efforts to improve its balance sheet, including raising new capital to continue the development of its therapeutic candidates. Specifically, on September 23, 2025, the Company received two letters from the Listing Qualifications Department of Nasdaq. The first letter confirmed the Company has regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The second letter confirmed the Company complies with the minimum market value of listed securities requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(b)(2). Nasdaq has advised that both matters are now closed. About Estrella Immunopharma Estrella is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing CD19 and CD22-targeted ARTEMIS® T-cell therapies to treat cancers and autoimmune diseases. Estrella’s mission is to harness the evolutionary power of the human immune system to transform the lives of patients fighting cancer and other diseases. To accomplish this mission, Estrella’s lead product candidate, EB103, utilizes Eureka’s ARTEMIS® technology to target CD19, a protein expressed on the surface of almost all B-cell leukemias and lymphomas. Estrella is also developing EB104, which also utilizes Eureka’s ARTEMIS® technology to target not only CD19, but also CD22, a protein that, like CD19, is expressed on the surface of most B-cell malignancies. For more information about Estrella, please visit www.estrellabio.com . Contact: Investor Relations Estrella Immunopharma, Inc. IR@estrellabio.com

title: The Strategic Value of Sustaining Services for OEMs
summary: Go beyond traditional maintenance. Discover how strategic sustaining services can enhance product value and streamline operations while protecting your brand and bottom line.
body_text: Home Blogs The Strategic Value of Sustaining Services for OEMs The Strategic Value of Sustaining Services for OEMs • October 31, 2025 • 8 min read Industry Insights | Servicing Share using Native tools Share Copied to clipboard Share on Mail (Opens in new window) Mail For many Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), sustaining services have traditionally been seen as a necessary but often overlooked part of the product life cycle. They’re generally viewed as a place where a product goes for reactive repairs, warranty claims and end-of-life support. This conventional approach, however, represents a missed opportunity. A modern, strategic view of sustaining services transforms this function from a reactive expense into a powerful driver of business growth, customer loyalty and operational efficiency. It’s about shifting your focus from simply maintaining assets to maximizing their long-term value. At Plexus, we believe a successful product journey doesn’t end at the point of sale. We’ve seen firsthand how a comprehensive, end-to-end approach to sustaining services can help OEMs build a more resilient business model. This starts by challenging the outdated notion that services are a last-resort function and instead, positioning them as a critical, forward-looking element of your overall strategy. The Strategic Shift: From Reactive to Proactive The limitations of a reactive “break-fix” model are clear: unpredictable downtime, soaring costs and the risk of damaging customer relationships. When a product fails, the reactive model kicks in, leading to a scramble for parts, logistics hurdles and service teams that are constantly putting out fires. This approach doesn’t just address a problem; it creates new ones, including inefficient use of resources and a fragmented customer experience. By shifting to a proactive model, OEMs can anticipate potential issues and address them before they impact a customer’s operations. Instead of waiting for a product to fail, a proactive model uses data and expertise to predict failures, optimize performance and extend a product’s life. It is the difference between a crisis management plan and a strategic asset management plan. This strategic shift empowers OEMs to take control of their product’s future. Instead of simply reacting to problems as they arise, a proactive approach allows for planned interventions and continuous improvements that ensure products remain reliable and effective in the field. This not only mitigates risk but also builds a reputation for dependability that sets an OEM apart in a competitive market. It’s about making a deliberate choice to invest in the long-term health of your product portfolio. The Three Pillars of Strategic Sustaining Services A strategic approach to sustaining services is built on three key pillars. When integrated, these pillars create a virtuous cycle of value, efficiency and customer satisfaction. 1. Optimize Costs Through Aftermarket Services To ensure long-term product success and customer satisfaction, a comprehensive suite of aftermarket repair and refurbishment services is essential. These services begin with a proactive approach to mitigating risk. It all starts with Diagnostics and Failure Analysis. By carefully examining failed products, it is possible to pinpoint the root causes of issues. This detailed analysis allows for more accurate predictions of future product failures, enabling you to address potential problems at the source and implement design or manufacturing improvements to prevent recurrence. This insight is invaluable for minimizing future service costs. When issues do arise, expert Aftermarket Repair: Level 1-4 services are critical for minimizing downtime and enhancing the customer experience. This tiered approach to repair handles everything from minor adjustments and field service fixes to complex, full component-level repairs and even depot-level board swaps. A dedicated partner with the capabilities to perform these complex fixes in a structured and efficient manner ensures that your products return to service quickly and reliably. For specialized fields like medical devices, Medical Device Decontamination is a critical service, ensuring safety for future use through professional cleaning, sterilization and secure patient data removal. A strategic partner will ensure these services are not just reactive but also informed by data, providing valuable feedback that can be used to improve product designs, manufacturing processes and supply chain management for the entire product line. 2. Extend Value and Asset Reliability A product’s value is not fixed at the moment of purchase; it can be enhanced and extended through its entire life cycle. Proactive sustaining services enable this through continuous upgrades and strategic improvements that keep a product relevant and reliable long after it leaves the factory. For instance, product life cycle extension strategies can include design for sustainability, part obsolescence management and redesigns that improve performance, add new features or lower operating costs. This helps OEMs maximize their return on investment and build a reputation for creating high-quality, dependable products. Think of it as a partnership with your customer’s asset. Instead of a one-time transaction, you are offering a long-term solution that continues to deliver value. This transforms the customer relationship from a single sale into a continuous partnership, based on a foundation of trust and demonstrated reliability. This continuous engagement also creates new revenue streams for OEMs. By offering upgrades, parts and service plans, a product can generate revenue far beyond its initial sale.
